title: Add residency-sentry service, data-governor role, and KMS escrow checks
author: Leah Kim
release_notes: Add a new residency-sentry background service and a data-governor operator role that gates KMS escrow usage by asserted key region; rollout is opt-in for Private installs and disabled by default for Hosted.
description:
Motivation: Customers in regulated industries require per-tenant enforcement of key residency checks and an operator-level 'data-governor' role that can observe residency decisions without broad cryptographic access. This PR adds a residency-sentry service that performs KMS escrow pre-checks (region assertion + policy allowlist) and surfaces immutable audit annotations. It also introduces a new operator role (data-governor) in the RBAC v2 model and a small gating shim so that KMS operations that would escape pinned regions are rejected earlier.

Summary of changes: 1) New background service `residency-sentry` (pkg/residency/sentry) that accepts signed residency assertions, verifies KMS key metadata against tenant-scoped residency profiles, and returns an allow/deny decision with an audit token. 2) RBAC: add `data-governor` role template and mapping rules in policy compiler (rbac/v2/templates.go) so platform operators can read residency decisions and audits without kms:Decrypt. 3) KMS integration: `pkg/kms/escrow_check.go` implements region gating hooks used by the runtime; on mismatch it returns structured error with audit hint to trigger tenant fallback. 4) Installer/Helm: chart additions to enable residency-sentry behind feature flag `residencySentry.enabled=false` by default for Hosted; default true for Private install profiles. 5) Console/docs: admin guide and runbook (docs/ops/residency-sentry.md) describing failure modes, mitigation, and migration path. 6) Tests: unit + integration mocks for KMS metadata and a small e2e that runs the sentry against a local k8s job.

Rollout plan: residency-sentry is gated behind a feature flag. We will ship with the flag off for hosted and on by default in the private-installer optional profile. The RBAC template will be available but not assigned to any principals until a gradual operator onboarding window. We will monitor the `residency.sentry.decision` metric, false-positive rate against known tenants, and any customer KMS error rates.

Security review: scoped review completed (SEC-213). The sentry only stores ephemeral audit tokens (signed, HSM-backed) and never persists raw encryption material. The data-governor role is read-only with explicit deny for KMS cryptographic APIs. Audit tokens are appended to request headers for traceability.

Backwards compatibility: Runtime will fallback to existing behavior if the sentry service is disabled. There are no breaking API changes for customers. The installer has a migration note: operators enabling this service must have KMS provider metadata (region) available via the provider registry.

Testing performed: unit tests for policy evaluation (rbac/v2), integration tests using test-kms stub (integration/kms_stub_test.go), helm chart lint and a small smoke e2e in CI job `ci/integration/residency-sentry`.

Related: Linear ENG-4821 (residency enforcement v2), SEC-213 (sentry design review), Jira SUP-1087 (support ticket uncovered need for operator-level audit visibility).
